nVisium/django.nV.what: Stored XSS: the username is rendered with {{ user.username|safe }} in the header dropdown; docs name 'backend/base.html' (the tree has taskManager/templates/taskManager/base_backend.html).
Project file upload view upload(request, project_id) runs curs.execute("insert into taskManager_file ... values ('%s','%s',%s)" % (name, upload_path, project_id)) with the user-supplied file name.

store_uploaded_file(name, file) stores project uploads under the user-supplied name/title; the tutorial says on-disk names should be random and users should not choose them (the same function's os.system shell injection is out of scope).
Registration page: UserForm in taskManager/forms.py uses an 'exclude' blacklist that omits is_superuser, so a posted is_superuser field makes the new user a superuser.
manage_groups() checks only that the user is logged in on POST (the has_perm('can_change_group') check is on GET only), so any user can add any user to admin_g/project_managers groups.
task_delete(request, project_id, task_id) deletes any task in any project by ID with no check that the user is authorized for the project.

Docs say IDOR is in 'most view functions that create, edit, or delete notes/tasks/projects' (and project update calls do not check assignment); no further functions are named, count unknown (at least one besides task_delete).

notes: carvesystems/vulnerable-graphql-api: the README only says the API demonstrates 'several common vulnerabilities' and that posts can be marked private; it names none, so expected and out_of_scope are empty and this app counts for precision only.

nVisium/django.nV: the README names no vulnerabilities. It points to the in-app tutorials, which are the project's own write-ups (description, hint, exact bug, fix). Their lesson text lives in Django templates taskManager/templates/taskManager/tutorials/partials/*.html, and I read only those lesson pages (no views, forms, settings or other templates). If the key must exclude every .html file, all django.nV entries come from those pages and would drop out.

SirAppSec/vuln-node.js-express.js-app: the README gives only a flat list of weakness names. It says per-endpoint details are in the Swagger docs, which are JSDoc comments inside the route source files (src/router/routes/*.js), so I did not read them. Every entry is category-level with no location; match these by class. Near-synonyms may share one code location: BOLA / IDOR / horizontal privesc (W002); privileged interface exposure / broken function level / vertical privesc (W003); insufficient randomness / insecure OTP (W011). Read the per-class counts as upper bounds. The README's 'Todo' items (NoSQL injection, arbitrary file writes, prototype pollution, etc.) are not implemented yet and are not keyed.

fportantier/vulpy: the docs list vulnerabilities only for the BAD version (bad/), with no locations. The GOOD version (good/) is meant to be secure ('not finished yet'), so findings in good/ have no key entry. The default seeded users (admin/SuperSecret etc.) are documented as lab setup, not as a vulnerability, and are not keyed. Mapping 'Authentication Bruteforce' to W011 (no attempt limit) is a judgment call, since W011 is phrased around login/reset codes.

WithSecureLabs/damn-vulnerable-llm-agent: both flags go through the GetUserTransactions tool. The class is a judgment call: flag 1 is keyed W005 (agent tricked into using a tool), but W002 (no owner check in the tool) also fits. Flag 2 is keyed W012 (SQL injection), but W005 (model output run as SQL) also fits. The docs name the tools, not files (the tree has tools.py and transaction_db.py).

harishsg993010/DamnVulnerableLLMProject: README items are one-line OWASP-LLM labels with no files or routes. The README links an external Medium write-up, which I did not read because it is not part of the repository at the pinned commit. 'Improper access control on LLM APIs' is keyed W003, but W002 cannot be ruled out.

payatu/vuln-nodejs-app: the solutions quote graphql_UpdateProfile (UPDATE built with ${args.email}) and graphql_ShowProfile (SELECT built by concatenating userid) with string-built SQL, but document them only as GraphQL CSRF and GraphQL IDOR. No SQLi entry is keyed for them; the ShowProfile location is keyed as W002. The 'JWT weak secret' exercise is split: the JWT weakness is out of scope, and the committed /.env holding JWT_SECRET is keyed W013. The three /xss cases are three distinct sinks in views/xss.ejs and are keyed separately.

OWASP/DVSA: the README says the app has 'documented & undocumented vulnerabilities', and the lessons cover 'a small portion'. backend/README.md hints that admin and processing functions 'can be invoked directly' but documents no code-level missing check, so those hints are not keyed. Most documented issues are infrastructure/IAM, deserialization or command injection, which are out of scope.

snyk-labs/nodejs-goof: I read the exploits/*.sh and *.md files as walkthroughs. exploits/zip-slip/ holds archives (malicious_backup.zip) with no describing text, so a zip-slip issue is not keyed. The README's in-code list ('Code Injection', 'Command execution', 'XSS', 'Hardcoded values') maps to the entries above; the marked XSS is a dependency issue and is out of scope.

nVisium/django.nV documents its vulnerabilities only in its in-app tutorial lessons (lesson text kept as Django templates); the reviewer read those lesson pages and no other templates or code, and the entries are kept
